question.text: The gas phase reaction <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><msub><mi>NO</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mfenced separators="|"><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></mfenced><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mo>→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mfenced separators="|"><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></mfenced></math> is an exothermic reaction. The decomposition of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mn>4</mn></msub></math> , in equilibrium mixture of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>NO</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mfenced separators="|"><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></mfenced><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi>and</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mo>(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mo>)</mo></math> can be increased by:

options.text: Addition of an inert gas at constant pressure
Addition of an inert gas at constant volume

solution.text:
2 NO2g→ N2O4 g                ∆H=(-)ve
By addition of inert gas at constant pressure, volume increases and thus, the pressure decreases. The reaction now moves in backward direction as this would increase pressure and hence, decomposition of N2O4 increases.
